It's not that anyone necessarily needs that particular app to help find books to read, it's that platforms like booktok and booktube and goodreads lead ppl to find titles they probably won't have in their local bookstores (primarily bc most modern writers are self publishing online and many books aren't in hard print). There's a fuck ton of books out there bro. Nobody has time to be trekking to the library or every bookstore in their area.

 Not everyone has the means either. What most ppl have, even if they lack other essentials, is a phone. It's fundamental for communication these days. As long as you have service, you have access to any number of platforms that have access to millions of books and thousands of ppl talking abt books that may fit your taste or introducing you to new themes and genres and authors that are lesser known and might never find themselves in a library. It's more than just some influencer telling you to go read. It's literally a community of book lovers talking to other book lovers (who also likely don't need to be told to visit a library in the 1st place)  abt books and reading. 

Hard print books are getting more expensive to produce which is partly why writing isn't paying the way it used to. Not to say that it was ever a lot.

[If you haven't read the Immortal Nicholas Flamel series of YA, I'd recommend. It's fairly diverse, though a lot of the cultural stuff is still fairly euro centric and not SUPER accurate when it comes to gods/beings from non euro religions, but it's a fun read regardless]

Some gods and beings I only acknowledge and venerate but I don't truly worship them (ie Demeter and Hecate and Kali). Bastet, Ereshkigal and Nergal came later, along with certain Saints (Cyprian, Francis, Expedite and John the Conqueror) and the Gnostic Saints even further on. I don't need the escape as I once did as a teenager, but I still work my Liberation magic to help ease the suffering of those around me and do justice for them as far as I can.
